finding_key: packages/backend/src/main.ts::rawbody capture keyed on an exact path string; any url variant (trailing slash, global prefix, proxy rewrite) makes every webhook 401 forever
evidence: Verified in the supplied packages/backend/src/main.ts: the verify hook captures rawBody only on exact, case-sensitive equality with '/internal/yorkie/events', while Express's default non-strict and case-insensitive routing still dispatches '/internal/yorkie/events/' or '/Internal/Yorkie/Events' to YorkieEventController.handleEvent — so rawBody is undefined and yorkie-signature.guard.ts:49-52 throws UnauthorizedException('Missing webhook signature') with no distinguishing log, exactly as claimed. The claim's global-prefix variant is hypothetical (the supplied bootstrap has no setGlobalPrefix), and the documented ops URL in docs/design/documents-last-modified.md matches byte-exactly, so the happy path works; a trailing slash entered by an operator is the realistic trigger. Impact when triggered is total-but-silent webhook rejection degrading list ordering to creation order plus misleading logs, not data loss, and it requires a misconfiguration, so I rate it minor rather than major. I could not execute the code (no checkout mounted); the Express strict/case-sensitive routing defaults are relied on from knowledge, but the file contents themselves were read directly.
